_comment: Human-approved alias resolutions. Decisions as data, with approver and evidence. Any name a machine cannot resolve is FLAGGED, never guessed; a human ruling is recorded here and becomes the written trail. Pattern approved 2026-07-28. roster_admissions records teams ADMITTED to a roster-locked state by league authority; alias decisions resolve NAMES, admissions add MEMBERS. merges records duplicate team rows collapsed by human ruling; alias decisions resolve NAMES, admissions add MEMBERS, merges remove DUPLICATES. KEEPER RULE: in a merge, the keeper is the row that CARRIES MORE — seasons, games, ranking entries, provenance — never the row that happened to be created first or by a particular source. blanchet_wa (kept the export row) and brophy_prep_az (kept the feed row) are worked examples. The 2026-07-29 brophy ruling kept the a7 row and is SUPERSEDED: it applied the rule correctly to a database in which brophy_az did carry more, and window #4-lite then inverted that. A merge direction is a fact about the rows on the day it is ruled, so a superseded entry stays in this file with its reason rather than being edited away. do_not_merge records pairs a human has ruled DISTINCT; scripts/reconcile-placeholders.js reads it and suppresses them, so a rejected candidate is never re-proposed. display_renames records display-name changes ruled by a human; the alias rows named in alias_preserved must continue to resolve afterwards, which scripts/strip-state-suffix-mountain-view.js asserts before committing.

merges.basis: same school reached from two directions by two sources; pre-dates the roster lock
evidence: Brophy College Preparatory, Phoenix AZ — universally shortened to 'Brophy Prep'
brophy_az seeded from a7-classification.json as an OREGON opponent, name 'Brophy College Prep'
brophy_prep_az seeded from the WHSBLA 2026 export as a WASHINGTON opponent, name 'Brophy Prep'
both rows are state=AZ; neither has team_seasons or ranking_entries
brophy_az holds the only game reference (Sunset @ Brophy College Prep, 2026-03-21)
merges.keep_rationale: brophy_az holds the game FK and carries the school's full canonical name
merges.note: Non-curated states have no roster lock, so nothing prevented this. Merging is a prerequisite gate before AZ rankings are ever enabled.
merges.superseded_reason: The KEEPER RULE is "carries more". When this was ruled on 2026-07-29 that WAS brophy_az: its evidence reads "neither has team_seasons or ranking_entries" and "brophy_az holds the only game reference". Window #4-lite imported Arizona's LaxNumbers season on 2026-08-04 and inverted both facts — brophy_prep_az now carries 23 games and 2 ranking entries against brophy_az's 1 and 0. The rule did not change; the database did, and this row is now a worked example of the rule pointing the wrong way.

merges.basis: same school reached from two directions; pre-dates the roster lock
evidence: Bishop Blanchet High School, Seattle — the WHSBLA export lists it as 'Blanchet'
bishop_blanchet_wa seeded from a7-classification as an OREGON opponent (Lake Oswego/Riverdale @ Bishop Blanchet, canonical_source=ohsla)
blanchet_wa seeded from the WHSBLA 2026 export as a MEMBER: 6 league games, wa_private for 2026 AND 2027, 1 ranking entry
the a7 row has no team_seasons at all
merges.keep_rationale: blanchet_wa carries far more — 6 games vs 1, two seasons vs none, a ranking row vs none
merges.note: Direction is OPPOSITE to the brophy merge, deliberately. See the keeper rule.

merges.basis: same school, same as before; the KEEPER RULE applied to the database as it is now rather than as it was in July
evidence: brophy_prep_az: 23 games, 2 ranking entries — the row LaxNumbers rates and the app currently serves as ranked
brophy_az: 1 game (Sunset @ Brophy College Prep, 2026-03-21, canonical_source=ohsla), 0 rankings, no team_seasons
the July ruling rested on "neither has team_seasons or ranking_entries" and "brophy_az holds the only game reference"; window #4-lite falsified both on 2026-08-04
brophy_prep_ii_az is a separate squad and is NOT part of this merge
surfaced by scripts/cross-state-audit.js as a direction-(A) mis-created row
merges.keep_rationale: brophy_prep_az carries 23 games and both ranking entries; keeping brophy_az would delete the ranked row and change a public slug the app already serves
merges.note: Replaying the recorded direction verbatim would have honoured the artifact and broken the rule the artifact cites. A decision is about a database state; when that state is falsified by a later window, the decision is re-made and both are kept.

merges.basis: one combined Boise program reached under two names; OHSLA writes the short name, the Idaho feed writes the combined one
evidence: borah_capital_id "Borah/Capital": 12 games, ranked
borah_id "Borah": 3 games, all against Oregon opponents (mt_view 2026-04-10, sprague and bend_caldera 2026-04-11), 0 rankings, no team_seasons
those three are the games docs/user-visible-changes.md change #4 describes as played against Borah/Capital — the notes and the data disagree today
surfaced by scripts/cross-state-audit.js as a direction-(A) mis-created row
merges.keep_rationale: KEEPER RULE: borah_capital_id carries 12 games and the ranking; borah_id carries 3 cross-border games and nothing else
merges.note: The alias matters more than usual here: OHSLA will keep writing "Borah", and after the resolver fix an unresolvable name is REFUSED rather than guessed — so without this alias those three games would stop importing instead of landing on the wrong row.

display_renames.ruling: Canonical display names are context-free; disambiguation is the out-of-state tag's job, derived per viewing context. The suffix was also wrong in WA's own context, where it stated the state redundantly.
display_renames.evidence: Only 1 of 159 teams carried a bracketed state in its display name.

game_identity_rulings.question: On 2026-04-10 a 12-13 loss to Borah appears twice: OHSLA #243 as Oregon mt_view, LaxNumbers #96806 as Idaho mountain_view_id. One game or two?
game_identity_rulings.ruling: ONE game. Oregon mt_view at home vs visiting Borah. Keep OHSLA #243; delete LaxNumbers #96806.

oracle_a.standing: his son's club — he was there that weekend
oracle_a.answer: Borah traveled to Bend and played three games across Apr 10-11, matching OHSLA's three fixtures exactly (mt_view 4/10; sprague and bend_caldera 4/11).

oracle_b.attempted: live fetch of Borah/Capital's LaxNumbers team page
oracle_b.result: BLOCKED — laxnumbers.com returns HTTP 403 from this machine (the Cloudflare block recorded in scripts/laxnumbers-probe.js). Not an independent re-fetch.
oracle_b.substitute: the already-imported LaxNumbers rows for Borah/Capital, which show exactly ONE 12-13 Mountain View fixture on 4/10 and a separate 12-3 on 3/04 — consistent with one game, not two.

game_identity_rulings.why_not_a_coincidence: Two oracles agree. A second 12-13 game against a different Mountain View on the same day would be coincidence; the firsthand account rules it out, and the imported feed shows only one.
game_identity_rulings.upstream_finding: LaxNumbers' Idaho page attributes Borah's ROAD game to mountain_view_id — the same bare-name collision this window fixes locally, occurring upstream in the source itself. We cannot fix their page; we can refuse to inherit it. Logged to source_conflicts and to docs/data-quirks.md.
game_identity_rulings.note: No deletion was made until both oracles reported. The audit carried this pair as an open finding in the meantime rather than letting it be forgotten.
